question: After a measurement lands, should the Measure tool stay in your hand or hand back to the arrow?
context: Found on the end-to-end walk (queue/audits/2026-09-02-redline-walk.json): taking a distance, a size, a gap and an alignment check cost seven presses of I because every landing returns to the arrow. This is the biggest repeated stop for someone redlining a whole screen.

options.label: Stay in hand
options.summary: After a size, gap, distance or guide lands, the ruler stays selected and the pointer stays a crosshair. You take the next measurement with the next click. Press V, Esc or click the arrow tool to put it down.
pros: Measuring five things is five clicks, not five presses of I plus five clicks
Matches how the ruler works in Photoshop and Figma: a tool stays until you change it
The mode pill is not re-raised on every landing, so there is less flashing
cons: Pressing I after a landing now cycles the mode instead of picking the tool up, which an old habit could trip on
A stray click after the last measurement can drop an unwanted caliper, undone with Command Z
options.mitigation: The landed measurement is still selected and shown in the inspector, so a single Esc or V returns to arrow when you are done.

options.label: Hand back to Select (today)
options.summary: Each measurement lands selected with the arrow tool active, as every other drawing tool does. Press I again for the next one; the mode you were in is remembered.
pros: Consistent with arrows, rectangles and text, which all hand back after one shape
The landed measurement is ready to drag or restyle at once
cons: A redline with many numbers costs a press of I before every one
The mode pill re-raises on each pickup, seven times on the walk for four measurements
options.mitigation: The mode is sticky, so each pickup is one press, never a hunt through the modes.

options.label: Stay for Size and Gap only
options.summary: The one-click modes, Size and Gap, keep the tool so you can click element after element; Distance and Alignment, which take several clicks or a drag, hand back to Select as today.
pros: Fast where it matters most: sizing and spacing a whole screen
Multi-step modes keep the familiar hand-back
cons: Two rules for one tool; which one applies depends on the mode you are in
Harder to explain in the mode pill
options.mitigation: The pill line for Size and Gap can end with the words and keeps measuring.
